summary: This is a sound single-area change that targets the two largest gaps at m=128 (pooler 25.2 vs 14.6 us floor, unpooler 20.0 vs 14.6). The incumbent nvjet times are very stable across 14 runs (pooler 24.1-25.9 us, unpooler 19.8-21.9 us), so the replaced kernel's own time is a clean readout and no companion run is needed. The main risks are whether Triton's wgmma mainloop runs near peak and how long the 64 KB-per-partial reduce tail takes, both of which can be measured for free in prepare().
justification: Mechanism: at m=128 the arithmetic intensity is 128 FLOP per weight byte, while the H200 ridge is about 206 (989 TFLOP/s / 4.8 TB/s). The shape is memory-bound, but only by about 1.6x (8.7 us of math vs 14 us of bytes). cuBLAS's pooler choice (64x64 tile, 2x1 cluster, 128 CTAs) reaches about 2.7 TB/s, and each CTA pulls 1 MB of x from L2 per 512 KB of weight. The proposed 128x128 tile over a 2048-wide K-slice halves the x traffic per weight byte (64 MB of L2 x reads per call instead of 128 MB) and still fills one wave of 128 CTAs. The arithmetic in the hypothesis checks out: 512 KB of weight plus 512 KB of x per CTA, 67 MFLOP per CTA, 128 KB of shared memory for 4 stages. About 64 KB of weight is in flight per SM, or about 8 MB across the GPU, well above the roughly 5 MB that Little's law needs at 4.8 TB/s. FINDINGS and the result files support the premise. Both rows are single nvjet kernels at 100% of shape time, with no splitKreduce node to remove, so the gain must come from the mainloop and not from launch savings. The unpooler argument is the same at SPLIT_K=2. The expected directions agree with TASK.md: only the two verify_16 rows change, and the verify_16 load is 1 of 6. Saving about 8 us out of about 76 us on that load gives about 1.11x on it and about +1.8% on the geomean, which is inside the 1.5% CI resolution, so the result must be read per shape and per kernel, as the hypothesis already says. WEAKEST LINK: the shape is co-bound. One wave of 128 CTAs on 132 SMs needs about 9.0 us of pure wgmma time per CTA at 100% of per-SM peak. A Triton cp.async (non-TMA) pipeline with BLOCK_K=64 typically reaches 60-75% of wgmma peak, which is 12-15 us of math, and that must overlap almost perfectly with about 16 us of weight streaming at 4 TB/s. There is little slack. Each stage also fetches only 128 B per weight row (BLOCK_K=64, rows 16 KB apart), the shortest contiguous run of any Triton stream measured here; LESSONS' best stream used BLOCK_K=256. The second weakest link is the reduce tail, which this epilogue never paid at m<=32. Each partial is now 128x128 fp32 = 64 KB, 8x the m<=32 case. The winning CTA reloads SPLIT_K partials serially: 256 KB for the pooler, 128 KB for the unpooler. At roughly 100-150 GB/s of per-SM L2 bandwidth that is about 1.7-2.5 us for the pooler and 0.9-1.3 us for the unpooler, on the critical path after the single wave. With a 16 us mainloop, the pooler's <=19 us target is reachable but not comfortable, and the unpooler's <=17.5 us target is plausible. A fallback to mma.sync would land near cuBLAS, a wash and not a disaster.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: this change replaces that dispatch for exactly these two rows. SGLang's side uses the same cuBLAS kernel, so the paired ratio is against the incumbent and is clean. Each shape is a separate CUDA graph with cold L2, so the cuBLAS path for other shapes cannot interact. Not a confounder.

router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: this change shares only the code pattern (direct transposed [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] addressing) and adds Triton warm-up in prepare() (compile time comes out of the 10-minute budget, about 2 more specializations). Router shapes are timed in separate graphs and have no runtime interaction with pooler or unpooler at m=128. Not a confounder.
router-hilo-at-m8: its router branch was replaced wholesale by the split-K router. No interaction. Not a confounder.
interference: No companion is warranted. A gain is unambiguous: the readout is the _bf16_tc_splitk_kernel time in top_kernels against nvjet times that sit in a 24.1-25.9 us band (pooler) and a 19.8-21.9 us band (unpooler) across all 14 runs, Triton reproduces within about 1%, and no landed hypothesis touches these rows. Only a loss would be ambiguous: wgmma fallback or a low-efficiency mainloop versus the reduce tail. A passing companion cannot separate those, because any run that skips or alters the reduce either fails correctness or changes the tail itself. Resolve it inside this run instead, at no cost in checks. In prepare() (untimed, 300 s budget), after warm-up: (1) print whether 'wgmma' appears in the compiled kernel's PTX (kernel.asm['ptx']) and print n_regs and n_spills. This replaces the 'check the PTX before the run' step that this GPU-less node cannot do. (2) Time, with torch.cuda.Event on synthetic x, the full kernel and a constexpr variant (REDUCE=False) that stores partials and takes the ticket but skips the winner's reload and sum. Print both times. Neither print is used by kernel_fn. The difference is the tail, and the printed log_tail attributes a loss to the mainloop or the reduce. Re-zero the counters after these timings, just as after warm-up. If the implementer prefers not to touch prepare(), proceed anyway: a loss then settles the 'Triton 128x128 wgmma at m=128' family well enough to decide the follow-up (a TMA weight stream or a larger BLOCK_K), which is the purpose of the sibling pooler-splitk2-tma-weight-stream.
rules_flags: None blocking. There are no host syncs, no branching on values, and no caching of anything derived from data. The workspace and counters are prepare()-allocated scratch that is fully rewritten (or self-reset) on every call, the same pattern that passed in pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore (08ec203e5717406e) and qkv-gate-triton-splitk4 (135ef6499875416a). Weights stay bf16 with no repack, accumulation is fp32 and the output is bf16, matching SGLang's precision. The single-nonzero power-of-two rows stay exact, because a fp32 sum of one nonzero product plus zeros is exact.

Minor: the counters are persistent mutable state across graph replays. Keep the property that every CTA takes exactly one ticket (no early exit) and that the winner resets with atomic_xchg. Re-zero the counters after warm-up and after any prepare-time timing.

Minor: the gate must stay on cfg m == 128 (or 65 <= m <= 128) with exact n/k checks. The correctness test 'm 130, layer unpooler' must keep taking cuBLAS, because BLOCK_M=128 does not loop over M and a widened gate would silently drop rows 128-129.
If prepare-time CUDA-event timing is added, it measures only our own kernel on synthetic inputs and does not patch or read harness timing. It should be fine, but keep it out of kernel_fn.
open_questions: Sequencing with the sibling qkv-gate-o-m128-wgmma-splitk-semaphore: it uses the same _bf16_tc_splitk_kernel design, so a wgmma fallback or tail problem would sink both. Should the sibling wait for this run to harvest (this one has the larger gap) instead of spending two checks on the same design risk at once? If both land, the shared kernel name and the _ws/_cnt state keys must be merged by hand.

Is BLOCK_K=64 forced by the 4-stage shared-memory budget? Three stages at BLOCK_K=128 (64 KB per stage, 192 KB, at the 227 KB limit before epilogue scratch) would double the contiguous run per weight row. That is a natural follow-up if the mainloop, not the tail, is the problem.

The verbatim epilogue makes the winner reload its own partial too. Keeping the winner's acc in registers and reloading only the other SPLIT_K-1 partials would cut the pooler tail by about 25% and the unpooler's by 50%, at the cost of a summation order that depends on which CTA wins (still correct, but not bitwise reproducible). This is a candidate stacked follow-up, not for this run.

Does Triton's epilogue convert the 128x128 fp32 accumulator through shared memory for the partial store? If so, 128 KB of pipeline buffers plus 64 KB of conversion scratch is about 192 KB. That fits, but check n_spills and occupancy in the printed diagnostics.
